Actors for amateur and FC2 codes may be fake names such as 「素人」. Ticking "Use AV-wiki to get actors' real names" asks AV-wiki for the actor's real Japanese name, which can then be translated with the mapping table!
Actor names are complicated and cannot simply be run through a translation engine. The main problems: inaccurate translation, several names per actor, inconsistent actor names for the same actor across codes, different sites using different names.
An actor-name mapping table solves these and keeps scraped actor names consistent.
How it works: after a scraped site returns the actor name, the matching keyword in the mapping table is looked up to map it to an output word.
The actor-name mapping table file is: mapping_actor.xml
· Windows path: \config dir\userdata\mapping_actor.xml (the config directory is set in [Settings] - [Other])
· Mac path: /config dir/userdata/mapping_actor.xml
You can open the file in a text editor and edit it yourself. The fields in the mapping table mean:
1. keyword: the match word (a comma before and after each name). After a site returns an actor name it is matched against the keyword names.
2. zh_cn/zh_tw/jp: the output words. When a keyword matches an actor name, the name in the matching language is output.

1. Feature overview

A Japanese-film metadata scraper. It works alongside local media managers such as EMBY, KODI and PLEX: the program fetches and classifies metadata, which those libraries then use to organise your local collection.

3.5. Videos with built-in subtitles

Name the file like ssni-xxx-c.mp4, ssni-xxx-C.mp4 or abp-xxx-CD1-C.mp4.


3.6. Multi-part videos

Name multi-part files with a part suffix, like ssni-xxx-cd1.mp4, ssni-xxx-cd2.mp4 or abp-xxx-CD1-C.mp4. Any -CDn/-cdn style suffix enables the multi-part feature. **-A, -B, -1 and -2 are NOT supported, because they are easily confused with the -C subtitle marker.**


3.7. Multi-part and subtitle order

In abp-xxx-CD1-C.mp4 the part comes first and the subtitle marker last; the subtitle marker must sit next to the extension, as in -C.mp4.


3.8. External subtitle files

A subtitle file only moves to the new directory together with the video if its name matches the video's. srt, ass and sub files are supported.

4. Settings reference


Full documentation: https://github.com/moyy996/AVDC/blob/master/README.md


4.1. Scrape mode / Organise mode

1. Scrape mode: fetch data by code - metadata, cover image, thumbnails and background image.

2. Organise mode: do not fetch anything; just rename each film to its code and file it under the actress's folder.


4.2. Symlink mode: run the program as administrator to use this mode.

Rather than moving the video after scraping, a symlink (like a shortcut) is created in the target directory - handy if you downloaded over PT and want to keep seeding while still scraping.

Note, however, that the result can only be displayed in the media library, not played from it.


4.3. Debug mode

Prints the code's metadata: cover, director, cast, plot summary and so on.


4.4. Excluded directories

Directories listed here are skipped when scraping a nested tree.


4.5. Video directory

The directory to organise; every video beneath it is walked, subdirectories included.


4.6. Naming rules

1. Directory naming: the folder name holding the video data. Nested directories and custom symbols are supported, e.g. [actor]/studio/number-[title].

2. Video title (in the media library): the title written into the .nfo, e.g. number-[title]. Custom symbols allowed.

3. Video title (local file): the name of the local video and image files, e.g. number-[title]. Custom symbols allowed.

4. Available fields: title, actor, studio, director, release (release date), year, number, runtime, series and publisher.


4.7. Proxy settings

1. Proxy

proxy=127.0.0.1:1080

The proxy line sets the local proxy address and port. Shadowxxxx/X and V2XXX local ports are supported; run the proxy client in global mode. A Japanese proxy is recommended.

If you keep getting 'Connect Failed! Please check your Proxy or Network!', check that the port number is correct, or delete the address and port after proxy= and switch the proxy client to global mode, or restart the machine, the proxy client and the network adapter.

2. Connection timeout

timeout=10

10 is the timeout in seconds; the valid range is 3-10.

3. Connection retry count

retry=3

3 is the number of retries; the valid range is 2-5.


4.8. Media library

If you use PLEX, install the XBMCnfoMoviesImporter plugin.


4.9. Excluded characters, directories and strings

1. Excluded characters: the given characters are deleted. For example \() removes \() when creating folders.

2. Excluded directories: for example failed,JAV_output - these are skipped when scraping multiple directories.

3. Excluded strings: removed before extracting the code, which improves the hit rate. Separate them with ','.


4.10. Site selection

You may scrape with all sites, or with specific ones (avsox, javbus, dmm, javdb, fc2club, mgstage, avbase, missav).

Try to avoid scraping with javdb alone: after roughly 30 entries JAVDB blocks your IP for a while.


4.11. Save log

When enabled, the log is written to a txt file in the Log directory of the program folder. One file per run; they can be deleted without affecting the program.


4.12. Move files after failure

If no film information can be scraped, either leave the video where it is or move it automatically to the failed-output directory.

<html><head/><body><p><b>创建软链接：</b><br/>:
Create symlink:
1. Symlinks suit network-drive users. A symlink is like a shortcut: a symbolic link pointing at the real file. It is tiny, can point across drives, and deleting it does not affect the original file (if the original is deleted the symlink stops working).
Note:
Windows: a symlink must be stored on a local disk (platform limit); the real file can be on a network drive or a local disk.
macOS: no problem.
Docker: the full path of the mounted directory must match the real directory's full path, so the symlink points at the real location and Emby can play it.
2. Network drives are affected by the network: slower reads and writes, more limits. When you create symlinks, a symlink file pointing at the network-drive video is created on a local disk and the scraped images are also stored locally, so Emby and Jellyfin load fast!
3. Scraping never moves, modifies or renames the original files; it only reads their paths to create the symlinks
4. After a successful scrape, symlink files are created and renamed following the scrape settings
5. On failure no symlink is created; to create symlinks for every file, go to [Tools] - [Symlink assistant] - [Create symlinks])
6. If the network drive already holds scraped content and you want to move the scrape information to a local disk, use the same tool and tick [Copy the scraped images and NFO files]
7. How to mount a network drive and scrape:
-1) Mount the network drive with a third-party tool such as CloudDriver, Alist or RaiDrive
-2) In MDCx set the folder to scrape to the network-drive video directory and the output directory to a local disk folder
-3) Choose [Create symlink] in the settings, configure the rest, save the configuration and click Start scraping
-4) Point the Emby/Jellyfin library path at the local folder the scrape saved to and scan
<html><head/><body><p><b>创建硬链接：</b><br/>:
Create hardlink:
1. Hardlinks suit PT users. PT users usually keep video files on a NAS and cannot change the original file information without hurting their upload ratio.
2. A hardlink points at the same disk index as the original file and must be on the same disk. With hardlinks you can keep scraped material separately on the same disk without touching the original file information.
3. Delete the hardlink and the original file is still there; delete the original file and the hardlink is still there. Only when both are deleted is the file deleted.
Note: macOS only allows hardlinks on a local disk (permissions); for a non-local disk choose to create a symlink instead. Windows has no such problem.
